gaps.sentence: The consultant will ___ us on every stage of the merger.
gaps.explanation: 'Advise' is the verb; 'advice' is the noun.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me a fascinating story about her childhood.
gaps.hint: telling a story to a person: ___ + person + story
gaps.explanation: 'Tell' takes a person as object: tell somebody a story. 'Say' does not take the listener directly.

gaps.sentence: He is very ___ to criticism and takes it personally.
gaps.hint: easily affected or hurt; pattern: ___ to
gaps.explanation: 'Sensitive to something' means easily affected or upset by it; 'sensible' means showing good judgement.

gaps.sentence: She gave me some useful ___ about buying a house.
gaps.hint: a noun is needed after 'some useful'
gaps.explanation: 'Advice' is the uncountable noun; 'advise' is the verb. 'Advices' is not standard English.

gaps.sentence: He ___ her on her presentation and her handling of questions.
I can still ___ the day we first met.
gaps.hint: to keep in your memory yourself
gaps.explanation: 'Remember' means to keep something in your memory; 'remind' means to make someone else remember.

gaps.sentence: The two brothers are ___ in appearance but not in character.
gaps.explanation: 'They are alike' — 'alike' follows the verb and cannot come before a noun.

gaps.sentence: The smell of hay ___ me of my childhood.
gaps.explanation: 'Remind somebody of something' — remember is not used with an object here.
